required.description: 0.1: spawn the crash worker, SIGKILL it, confirm the shared container is still up and a fresh client connects.
0.1: pg_terminate_backend drops a targeted backend's connection and the dedicated pool recovers (reconnects with a new backend pid).
0.3: a query against a deliberately-stalled backend is bounded by a 1.5s override of the suite watchdog and throws a typed SuiteWatchdogTimeoutError before G7's 120s, not a hang.
0.3: withSuiteWatchdog with NO explicit override applies SUITE_WATCHDOG_MS as its default bound (proven fast via fake timers, so the default is wired without a real 60s wait).
0.2: without UMBRADB_CRASH_HOOK the worker performs an ordinary uninterrupted save and exits 0.
0.2: the before-commit hook pauses after the manifest INSERT is issued, before COMMIT, and emits its readiness signal (incl. the worker backend pid); nothing is visible.
0.2: the in-critical-section hook pauses inside a held withLease; exactly one class-2 advisory lock with objid = hashtext(leaseKey) is held.
0.2: the after-data-commit-before-cursor hook runs TWO real ops (save then cursor) with a pause between; killed at the pause it leaves data durable and the cursor absent (watermark behind data).
0.2: the after-cursor-before-data hook runs TWO real ops (cursor then save) with a pause between; killed at the pause it leaves the cursor durable and the data absent (T5 unsafe reference case).

0.2 (test-honesty): the SAME co-transactional data->cursor flow run to completion WITHOUT a kill lands BOTH data and cursor — the negative control proving the killed T5 runs' absences are caused by the crash, not by a missing op.

T1 (Task 1.1): SIGKILL at before-commit leaves no complete=true manifest at the interrupted seq; the prior seq still loads+hash-verifies; no orphan junction rows; negative control (no kill => visible complete manifest).

T2 (Task 2.1): Postgres killed mid-save => the in-flight save rejects with a typed ConnectionError (not a raw driver error); after recovery the checkpoint is all-or-nothing and load(latest) returns correct bytes.

T2 (Task 2.2): the lost-COMMIT-ack state built by the sanctioned simulation (a provably-committed save re-invoked with identical content) yields a benign identical-content duplicate at the next seq; load(latest) correct either way; static check that save is excluded from any auto-retry allowlist.

T5 (Task 3.1, depends on G5): killed at after-data-commit-before-cursor, the durable watermark is never ahead of durable data (every write batch with cursor <= durable watermark is present in durable data).

T5 (Task 3.1, depends on G5): replay from the durable cursor converges on a current state equal (current-state equality predicate: kv_current + latest complete checkpoint payload + watermark values; excludes kv_history/version) to a fault-free in-repo reference replay of the same write-batch sequence.
T5 (Task 3.2, depends on G5): the watermark-never-ahead invariant holds under synchronous_commit = on.

T5 (Task 3.2, depends on G5): under synchronous_commit = off with an UNCLEAN postmaster kill (pg_ctl stop -m immediate / in-container kill -9), a lost tail of acknowledged commits is acceptable but an inverted durability order (cursor durable, data not) is a failure.
T3 (Task 4.1): after a lease-holder is SIGKILLed, a fresh process's withLease on the same key acquires immediately (bounded wait, no wedge) and pg_locks shows the class-2 advisory lock gone.

Soak (Task 5.1): a sustained concurrent mix at a declared envelope (10^5-10^6 chunks) samples a named P1-P10-derived SQL-observable invariant set DURING the run (gapless per-key version, only complete manifests loadable, no dangling junction, watermark <= max durable data); end state equals a fault-free reference; each GC-pass duration is recorded and bounded by GC_PASS_WATCHDOG_MS (no perf threshold gates).

Load-under-prune (Task 5.2): a FORCED, verified interleave lands the prune COMMIT inside load's open REPEATABLE READ snapshot window; load returns correct bytes and never raises ChunkIntegrityError/ChunkMissingError for a surviving checkpoint; negative control (un-snapshotted read of a reclaimed chunk DOES raise ChunkMissingError) fires.

P3 anchor (Task 6.1): the existing P3 replay/fold-equivalence property (getAt matches a from-scratch fold of the put sequence) is the differential gate's fold-equivalence anchor, satisfied WITHOUT importing the replaced store. Task 6.1 tags the existing P3 test with this id; no new test code.

Differential fault-schedule (Task 6.2, depends on G5): a SEEDED (reproducible, no Math.random) schedule mixing the G9 faults T1/T2/T5 across write batches, re-syncing from durable state after each fault, converges to a current state EQUAL (current-state predicate: full kv_current + full watermarks + latest complete checkpoint payload; excludes kv_history/version) to a fault-free in-repo reference run (a replay via UmbraDB's own adapters — NOT reference-merge.ts, which is transaction-history-merge only; no foreign consumer/indexer import, verified by an in-test import audit) of the same schedule. Mandatory negative control: a deliberately-broken variant that drops a committed range makes the equivalence assertion FIRE.

Co-transactional G5 crash (change-level audit BLOCK 1): saveAndAdvance — the single-transaction save+cursor combinator — SIGKILLed BETWEEN its internal checkpoint-data write and its cursor write (both inside the ONE uncommitted tx, paused via a test-only query observer over saveAndAdvance's own sql, NO src change) leaves NEITHER the checkpoint NOR the watermark advance durable (all-or-nothing), and a fresh saveAndAdvance on the same key then lands seq 1 committing both; a no-kill co-tx-full-flow control lands BOTH. Crash-tests G5 atomicity DIRECTLY (the two-transaction T5 tests never crash saveAndAdvance itself).

Differential negative control (change-level round-3 BLOCK 3): the mandatory dropped-range negative control - a deliberately-broken variant that skips one faulted batch's recovery so a committed range is genuinely dropped - makes the SAME current-state equality predicate the positive test relies on FIRE (throw). Required-enforced so deleting/skipping the control (or weakening assertCurrentStateEqual) turns the gate red by id.

Differential reference import-cleanliness (change-level round-3 BLOCK 4): a static audit that the in-repo reference imports nothing outside the repo - directly AND through its relative-import closure - catching bare import, dynamic import() and require(), and rejecting any @midnightntwrk/indexer/consumer/wallet specifier. Required-enforced so skipping/removing it turns the gate red by id.

00024-02 C6 (spec 00024 FR-013, Q7, Q13, US1 scenario 4b): Level 3 is TRIED with the exact compiler the bundle names, driven against a stand-in for the Compact CLI (helpers/fake-compact.mjs - CI has no compiler; it answers 'compile +<v> --version' and 'compile +<v> --trace-search ... <src> <out>' as compact 0.2.0 does and writes a recorded compile's output): the reference-built bundle passes with the reference's compared items (3 keys, contract/index.js, compiler/contract-info.json) and the locally generated keys per circuit; exactly two calls are made - the version probe and the compile with +0.34.0 and --trace-search - in a private directory holding the LISTED files only, with COMPACT_PATH removed, both directories removed afterwards; a bundle naming 0.33.0 (not installed) is not_run 'compiler 0.33.0 unavailable (...)' and never compiled (the reference reports versionMismatch instead - policy, audit F4), and a missing toolchain is not_run; a regenerated index.js, a missing key, an extra produced key, another key and another contract-info.json each fail; a compile error fails while the compiler's environment failing (proving parameters) is not_run; a trace read outside the bundle or of an unlisted file, and an unreadable trace line, fail, while '...not found' lines are ignored; the positive control fails a source that imports by name with no trace line; the deadline ends a slow compile as not_run within 5 s; unbounded compiler output fails; disallowed flags, an unlisted / traversing / missing compact.interface and a missing package.json fail before any compiler call; --feature-zkir-v3 is passed through. Non-governed and environment-gated beside it: the REAL host compiler reproduces the bundle exactly, reports 0.33.0 not_run, and fails an edited source on index.js. Negative controls: keeping COMPACT_PATH, or skipping the trace confinement, fails the test. compact.interface is resolved as the reference resolves it (02-E audit E2-F5): src/./X, ./src/X and src/../src/X compile the listed source; an absolute path or one leaving the bundle is refused before the compiler runs; a backslash is not rewritten. A read boundary BEFORE the compiler runs (E2-F6): a listed source whose quoted import/include names an absolute path, a path leaving the bundle, or one with a backslash is 'failed' and the compiler is never started; comments and relative in-bundle names are not refused. Whose failure a failed compile is, a PROBE compile of a known-good contract decides, never any text (E2-F7 / E2-R2C): the probe fails too -> 'not_run' (also for an unknown wording, and for a bundle whose README mentions 'data provider'); the probe compiles -> 'failed' (also for a diagnostic worded like an environment failure, e.g. a source named zkparams, or an echoed import './data provider'). The real-compiler suite compiles the probe. Round 2 (E2-R2D): compact.interface and the directives are resolved against the REAL private directory - ../bundle/src/X and import "../../bundle/Stolen" are refused (no fictitious root to re-enter) - and only the sources the compile reaches are examined: a listed but unused source importing /outside does not fail Level 3. Round 3: the reachable walk is linear (E2-R3B: one import repeated 600 000 times, 7.8 MB, walked in < 2 s - each file once, each distinct name once) and follows unquoted imports to the file next to the importer (E2-R3F: import Evil; + Evil.compact importing /outside is refused before the compiler). Level 3 never throws (E2-R3C, E2-R4D): a probe that cannot be prepared (a missing temp root) is 'could not be prepared (ENOENT)', and anything unexpected inside Level 3 (an injected probe that throws ENOSPC) is Level 3's own not_run, so the passed Levels 1-2 are kept; cleanup failures are ignored. Round 4: a selective import from an unquoted module (import { marker } from Evil;) is followed, a built-in (CompactStandardLibrary) never is - a listed file sharing its name is not examined.

00024-02 C7 (spec 00024 FR-010, Q14, US1 scenario 2; derivation P2): end to end - scanner -> drain outside the scan's transaction -> guarded HTTP to a real local host (test-only bypass) -> Level 2 on a stub provider -> Level 3 on the stand-in compiler: the first publication is verified L1/L2/L3 in one drain, with the [B] PR #6 verification record (publication, observation, provider limits, state + entry points, operations, artifact identities, compiler and build inputs, witnesses, levels, completed level, limits, 'nothing executed'), its history row and its re-check time; a NEWER publication whose index.json hash is not its commitment becomes current and is FAILED at L1 with one HTTP request, while the verified older one stays historical with its own last result, is no longer scheduled and is never re-checked; in one block the later transaction's publication is current although its event ids are lower, and both get their one check, the current first.

00024-02 C7 (spec 00024 FR-011b, US1 scenario 2b, Q14): nothing is due before TOKEN_INTERFACE_RECHECK_MS; after it the current publication is re-verified and, the host now serving other bytes for a listed file (a breached URL), it is FAILED at L1 naming the file, with verified_until = the time the earlier verified result held, the next re-check scheduled, and no rollback (it stays current, the older publication historical); the history records initial/recheck/on_demand triggers; verify-interfaces --address (verifyInterfaceNow) checks on demand, the restored host gives verified again with verified_until cleared; an unknown contract has no interface; a stalled host past the deadline is 'unchecked' (never failed) with attempts counted and a 30 s backoff, and the retry verifies and resets the attempts; then the host goes away (HTTP 503) and at the next re-check the current VERIFIED publication is 'unreachable' (02-C9, owner Q25) - level 0, l1/l2/l3 not_run, no failed level, reason 'the host did not deliver: ...' - with verified_until = its last verified check, retried after the first backoff, still current.

00024-02 C7 (spec 00024 FR-012, Edge Cases): a MaintenanceUpdate of the contract scanned in a later transaction marks its current interface 'stale' (last result kept, generation bumped, due now; the scan counts it); the drain re-verifies it (trigger 'stale') against the new state and, a key having changed, it FAILS at L2 with verified_until; a maintenance update scanned WHILE a check is in flight makes that check's result DISCARDED (generation guard; the row stays stale and uncounted) and the next drain verifies it; a maintenance update in a failed transaction or of a contract without an interface marks nothing; a never-checked publication stays pending with its generation bumped. Negative control: without the generation guard the raced result overwrites the stale and the test fails.

00024-02 C7 (UC-2, spec 00024 FR-001/FR-010, US4 scenario 3): a bundle URL longer than 224 bytes is published as a 512-byte payload in two parts of ONE intent -> one publication of 2 parts (part ids 10, 11) whose decoded URL is the whole URL, verified L1/L2/L3 end to end; the same two parts in two intents are two one-part packages, each judged alone on its own bytes - the first names a truncated URL (HTTP 404: unreachable, 02-C9), the second has no commitment and no URL (not a URL: unfetchable) - and the later one (P2) is current.

00024-02 C8 (spec 00024 §5, FR-010, FR-015 additive, FR-016b): over real HTTP on a database the scanner and the verification drain filled (four contracts: A published a good bundle then a broken one, B a good one, D (02-C9) a URL its host does not serve, C one not yet checked) - GET /v1/interfaces lists the three newest current publication first with status/level/levels/url/publications and origin, filters on status (unreachable -> D; 400 naming the seven statuses, unreachable included, for 'historical'), keyset-pages with limit/cursor and refuses a foreign cursor; GET /v1/contracts/:a/interface shows A's newest publication as current and FAILED (failed level 1, reason, payload length and SHA-256, check history) with the older verified one as historical carrying its own result, and B's verified interface with files, keys (sha256, L2 row) and circuits (rendered types), compiler, build, witnesses, state and the verification record - every interface value with origin public-interface and the publication as evidence; 404 for a contract without an interface, 400 for a malformed address; GET /v1/contracts/:a/interface/events lists every publication newest first with its role and own result, paged; Token.interface (additive) is on the minted token of A with its own origin while the token's origins keep exactly their eight 00024-01 fields and the built-ins carry null; the single-token and contract routes carry the interface; D's interface is 'unreachable' at level 0 with l1/l2/l3 not_run, no failed level, reason 'the host did not deliver: ...', no verifiedUntil, a next check scheduled and its origin; /internal/status counts interfaces, publications and current ones verified/failed/waiting/unavailable/unreachable, the five adding up to interfaces. Negative control: files served without their origin fail the test. An ITEM of an interface (file, key, circuit) cites its publication by identity only - no URL, no part ids - so a response is not amplified by the publication (02-E audit E2-R3D): a 20 000-byte URL with 1 000 files, 998 keys and 500 circuits gives a body under 3 MB with the URL once (the interface's own url field); round 4 (E2-R4B): no origin evidence repeats the URL, and Token.interface / a contract's interface are {status, level, ...} without it (spec §5), so the contract route of such a publication does not contain the URL.

00024-02 C (testing on 02-B5's real bundles; spec 00024 US1 Independent Test and scenarios 3-6, 4b): the six LSUNPI fixture bundles of mip-public-interfaces dd9d95f (fixtures/interfaces/b5-bundles, built by the patched public-interface-deploy-check with compactc 0.34.0) - after checking the recorded inputs (the state's digest, each payload's commitment/URL/parts, each index hash, file count and bundle size against cases.json) - each go through the indexer's whole pipeline (fetch guard over real HTTP, Level 1, Level 2 on LSUNPI.state.hex, Level 3 tried on the stand-in compiler with the trace lines a real compile prints) and end exactly as cases.json expects: valid -> verified L1/L2/L3 (9 circuits OK, 21 requests: index.json + the 20 listed files); tampered-file -> failed at L1 on src/generated/LSUNPI.compact; wrong-hash -> failed at L1 after exactly ONE request; over-size-cap -> unchecked under its 1 MiB cap with nothing past index.json (verified under the default caps); loopback-host -> unfetchable with private hosts refused (the production default) and no request; compiler-not-installed -> verified at L1/L2 with L3 not_run 'compiler 0.33.0 unavailable'.

00024-02 C9 (owner decision Q25 'unreachable (exponential fallback)', spec 00024 Key Entities, upstream log UC-13): the retry delay after a check that reached no conclusion is base * 2^(n-1), capped - with base 1 s / cap 8 s: 1, 2, 4, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8 s; the defaults 30 s doubling to the 1 h cap; never beyond the re-check interval; attempt 0 is the base and a huge attempt count gives the cap (2^n overflow); TOKEN_INTERFACE_RETRY_BASE_MS / TOKEN_INTERFACE_RETRY_CAP_MS default to 30000 / 3600000, override through loadConfig, reach the drain through drainDepsFromConfig, and are refused naming the variable when below 1000, not a number, or the cap below the base (zod); end to end through the scanner and the drain against a real local host that never delivers - HTTP 503, a reset connection, nothing served (404), a redirect loop (> 3 redirects), a gzip Content-Encoding, HTTP 500, HTTP 503, one per attempt - every check is 'unreachable' (level 0, l1/l2/l3 not_run, no failed level, reason 'the host did not deliver: index.json: ...' naming the cause), requests nothing past index.json, never reads the contract state, counts attempts 1..7, schedules the next check at exactly 1, 2, 4, 8, 8, 8, 8 s, and is not due one millisecond early; the history is initial then six retries, all unreachable at level 0; the record says completedLevel 0 with Level 1 not_run (outcome unreachable). 00024-02 C9 (owner decision Q25: 'a later delivery restarts verification at Level 1'; spec 00024 Key Entities, FR-011b; upstream log UC-13): a publication whose URL its host does not serve (HTTP 404) is 'unreachable' after its first check - level 0, l1/l2/l3 not_run, no failed level, no verified time, only index.json requested, the contract state never read, retried after the 1 s base; the host then serves the bundle and the retry, at exactly that time, verifies it L1/L2/L3 fetching index.json first and then every listed file (Level 1 from the start), attempts reset, back on the re-check timer; at the next re-check a listed file is missing on the host: 'unreachable' naming that file (not failed), verified_until = the last verified time, not due before the backoff; the file restored, the retry verifies it again from Level 1 with verified_until cleared; history initial/unreachable, retry/verified, recheck/unreachable, retry/verified. Negative controls: dropping 'unreachable' from the retried statuses (re-check timer instead of backoff), or reporting HTTP non-2xx as 'unfetchable', fails the test.

00024-02 E2 (Codex audit round 1, E2-F1; spec 00024 FR-011): a NUL in index.json's uncommitted compiler.flags gives a Level 1 compiler-mismatch reason that quotes it; the drain stores that publication 'failed' at L1 with the NUL replaced by U+FFFD (reason, history) and verifies the next publication in the SAME pass; a result the database refuses for any other reason (a test trigger) is replaced by an 'unchecked' internal-error result on its retry backoff and the queue moves on. Also E2-F4 / E2-R2B: a publication that passes Level 1, verified with INDEXER_HTTP carrying a credential (userinfo, path key, query, fragment), reaches the state request, which fetch refuses quoting that URL: stored 'unchecked' at Level 1 with a reason and report (and history) that carry no credential; the provider named by its origin only. Round 4 (E2-R4C): bundle-controlled text is bounded where it is stored - a 100 000-character compact.compiler gives a reason (and its history row) of at most 2 000 characters, the 'N characters omitted' marker included and exact (the bound is idempotent, E2-R5B), and record diagnostics of at most 8 192; DATA is never cut (E2-R5A): two committed 8 193-character paths stay exact and distinct in the record. Also E2-R7B: a publication whose host answers HTTP 101 is 'unreachable' and the next publication is verified in the same drain pass.

00024-02 E2 (Codex audit rounds 1-2, E2-F2 / E2-R2A; spec 00024 FR-011b): overlapping checks of one publication are ordered by a TICKET each draws from the database sequence public_interface_check_tickets when it starts - a periodic re-check A that has the honest bytes is still at Level 2 when the host is breached and an on-demand check B, started later on the SAME clock value, stores 'failed' at L1 with verified_until; A then finishes 'verified' and is SUPERSEDED (counted as discarded, not written, not in the history): the row keeps B's failure, times and schedule; a check started later on a clock BEHIND the stored result is still written (ticket order, not clock order). 00024-03 B6 (spec 00024 US6, FR-016, FR-016b): the served page script, evaluated in node:vm with a minimal document (no DOM dependency), on recorded API payloads (test/fixtures/ui, GET-captured from the 02 review stack at c29d7d4) and synthetic ones built from them: every value of the token and contract views of SNEB18, LMOON18, LSUNPI, UPROMPI and SSTARPI, of every one of the seven publication statuses (current and historical), of 02-D's seven fixture outcomes, of a 262 112-byte URL (1 024 parts) and of a contract with no interface, has an origin whose label is one of the five (MIP-0018 declaration, Public interface, Chain observation, Derived by this indexer, Not available), with a rule (derived) or a reason (none), and every evidence link resolves (a transaction the payloads name, the contract, the token, or a section the drawn view has; a public-interface value links its contract's interface section); every model item is drawn marked data-o with its own chip (label; link to its first evidence); SNEB18 name = 'MIP-0018 declaration' (tx, block 221, segment, 1 part), metadata 'MIP-0018 declaration, 3 parts'; LSUNPI name/symbol 'Not available (no declaration)', repository MIP-0018, interface 'failed at L1'; LMOON18 description '2 parts' with P1 named and the earlier Null and text listed newest first; every status badge known, the list's interface column per status (no interface part badge since 03-E1a F4), SNEB18's '3 parts'; the maximal URL shown head…tail (<= 101 chars) with its length and copied whole; a bounded diagnostic shown exactly as served; all five origin kinds met. Hardened by the 03-E1a Codex audit (E1a-F15, R2E-R3C: every drawn evidence line equals the model's links; derived section links expected at the token's own route; no distinctive piece of the payload - a text of 4+ characters, a hash head, a number of 2+ digits - is drawn outside a marked element; the heading's status, symbol, kind, privacy, storage, decimals, name and family are each one marked occurrence with its own chip): the script runs in the small browser of test/helpers/ui-page.ts (listeners, fetch, clipboard, hash navigation, scrolling kept); where the API gave a value an origin, the item has that origin kind and its first link is the evidence THAT origin names (computed from the payloads alone); every drawn occurrence carries its chip; no table value cell is drawn outside a marked element; boot on #/contract/<address>/interface scrolls to the section, a token-view evidence link navigates and scrolls, the URL copy control copies all 262 112 characters. E1a-F3: bundle fields the API passes through as published (package.json compact.language / runtime / interface / flags) that are objects without a callable toString ({"toString": null}) are drawn as their JSON (txt(), never String()), and a view that still cannot be drawn shows 'this view could not be drawn' instead of throwing out of render().
